claim: LLM alone beats unaided physicians on written-case differential generation: NEJM CPC top-10 59.1% vs 33.6% (McDuff, 302 cases); 78.3% in differential for o1 on 143 CPCs (Brodeur); 64% for GPT-4 on 70 cases (Kanjee).
agent_test: Run our agent vs its own plain single pass on CPC-style cases at equal tokens; score top-10 in differential.

claim: Giving clinicians an LLM raised their differential quality in the McDuff study (top-10 51.7% vs 36.1% unaided, 44.4% with search) but assisted clinicians stayed below the LLM alone (59.1%).
agent_test: Compare scaffold-assisted vs unassisted second-pass lists on the same cases.

claim: In the Goh 2024 RCT, access to GPT-4 did not improve physician diagnostic reasoning (+2 points, CI -4 to 8, P=.60) while GPT-4 alone scored 92% vs 74% for the control group.
agent_test: Reproduce the contrast: agent alone vs a plain prompt; the output must be usable by the next stage, not merely available.

claim: The human-plus-LLM benefit is not stable across studies: Goh 2024 +2 points (null), Goh 2025 management reasoning +6.5 points (CI 2.7-10.2), McDuff about +15 points top-10. Task type, tool and user training differ.
agent_test: Not directly testable on an agent; treat as warning that handing output to a weaker consumer loses value.
gap_search_note: Gap search 2026-11-01: Wang 2026 meta-analysis (k=2 per outcome) is imprecise; no same-design replication of Goh 2025 found; AMIE and cardiology trials are different systems.

claim: Physician plus LLM roughly equals LLM alone in management reasoning (43.0% vs 43.7%, diff -0.9, CI -9.0 to 7.2): the human adds no measurable correction on top of the model.
agent_test: In an agent with a self-check stage, measure whether the check ever turns a correct answer wrong or a wrong one right at equal tokens.

claim: Real-user performance falls far below model-alone performance: LLMs alone named relevant conditions 94.9% of the time, users with the LLM under 34.5%, below control (47.0%).
agent_test: Measure our agent when a lossy simulated user supplies the case vs full-information run.
gap_search_note: Gap search: Bean's simulated users scored higher than humans and barely predicted human scores; control figure 47.0% for conditions (43.0% is the disposition rate).

claim: LLMs are weaker when they must gather information themselves: Hager et al. found 12-13 point drops from full-information to autonomous mode and 16-25 points below hospitalists; Qiu et al. found R1 71.8% (1-turn) vs 89.8% (oracle information).
agent_test: Compare agent with all facts given vs agent that must ask for facts, at equal token budget.
gap_search_note: Gap search: MediQ (GPT-4 79.7 to 54.5 on iMedQA), neurosurgery conversion (GPT-4o 89.0 to 60.9 MC, 78.4 to 30.3 FR), AgentClinic all show elicitation loss for 2023-25 models; no o3-class test with a lossy patient.

claim: Order and amount of information, and instruction wording, change open-model diagnostic accuracy by large amounts (order up to 18 points; withholding information gives +18.5 to +21.6; wording -10.6 to +7.0).
agent_test: Shuffle the order of case facts and check whether agent accuracy moves less than the plain model.

claim: Structured multi-role orchestration around a model (MAI-DxO) raised accuracy 78.6 to 81.9% and cut cost $7,850 to $4,735 on SDBench; budgeted 79.9% at about $2,396; ensemble 85.5%. Generalist physicians scored 19.9% at $2,963.
agent_test: Add a challenger operator and cost-aware test chooser to our agent; compare at equal tokens.
gap_search_note: Gap search: Nori has no per-role ablation and no equal-token control; token-matched work elsewhere (d03) shows multi-agent can hurt on sequential tasks.

claim: Gains from structured orchestration are larger for weaker models; for strong reasoning models (o3, o4-mini) the main effect is lower cost, not higher accuracy.
agent_test: Test the scaffold on a weaker and a stronger base model and compare the delta.
gap_search_note: Gap search: restated from Nori; no new independent source.

claim: Prompting for an analytic or differential-diagnosis style does not help and can hurt: GPT-3.5 differential 38% vs CoT 46%; GPT-4 shows no significant change (72-78% vs 76%).
schema_part: O2 (do not force one reasoning style)
agent_test: Compare plain CoT vs forced-differential prompt vs our scaffold on free-response questions at equal tokens.
gap_search_note: Gap search: bias-prompt studies (not forced-differential prompts) show debiasing instructions help GPT-4 and 2025-era reasoning models; forced-differential on current models still untested.

claim: Benchmark knowledge scores do not predict interactive or real-case performance: models beat MedQA benchmarks in 20/20 scenarios yet users failed (Bean); only 5% of 519 LLM health studies used real patient data (Bedi).
agent_test: Do not validate the agent on exam-style items alone; include interactive and open-ended cases.

claim: LLM advice carries automation-bias risk: physicians given flawed LLM advice scored 73.3% vs 84.9% with correct advice (-14.0, CI -19.7 to -8.3).
agent_test: Plant a wrong suggestion in the agent's own context and measure whether its check catches it.
gap_search_note: Gap search: Qazi abstract gives adjusted -14.0 (CI -18.9 to -9.1), earlier line b24 gave CI -19.7 to -8.3; copilot simulation (n=13) found non-significant over-reliance (AOR 2.08, P=.09).

claim: Comparison with physicians depends on which physicians: pooled generative AI is not significantly different from non-experts (+0.6) but is 15.8 points below experts (P=.007); newer models close the gap.
agent_test: Report agent results against both novice-level and expert-level baselines.

claim: LLM top-1 lags top-10 by a wide margin on CPC (29.2% vs 59.1%; 52% vs 78.3%): models generate the right idea more often than they rank it first.
agent_test: Measure top-1 vs top-10 for the agent; test a rerank stage at equal tokens.
gap_search_note: Gap search: a perplexity reranker reached only AUC 0.666 on case reports; no CPC rerank study found.

claim: Conversational history-taking AI (AMIE) beat primary-care physicians on 28 of 32 specialist axes and 24 of 26 patient-actor axes with higher DDx accuracy, in text chat with patient actors.
agent_test: Compare interactive agent with a lossy simulated patient vs plain model.

claim: Older rule-based differential generators scored 1.70 to 3.45 of 5 (Isabel and DxPlain best, 36 cases). Modern LLMs exceed these on CPC cases, but the test sets differ, so no direct comparison exists.
agent_test: Context only.

claim: Training-data contamination does not explain the CPC results: o1 scored 79.8% before vs 73.5% after the training cutoff (P=.59), and McDuff's no-overlap subset gave 55.4% top-10.
agent_test: Use post-cutoff cases in any agent evaluation.
gap_search_note: Gap search: Nori's 56 post-cutoff test cases scored at least as high as the 304 set, and 2026 BiasMedQA work flags contamination in Gemini-2.5-Flash on unpublished prompts. Still no direct pre/post comparison for reasoning models on real records.

claim: Physician-vs-LLM comparisons rest on very few cases and raters: Goh 2024 used 6 vignettes and 3 graders (kappa 0.66); the o1 vs physician landmark comparison was P=.055, not significant.
agent_test: Use at least 50 cases and bootstrapped intervals in our own tests.

claim: Reasoning models improve diagnosis beyond GPT-4: o1 78/80 perfect R-IDEA vs GPT-4 47/80 and attendings 28/80; o3 78.6% on SDBench vs GPT-4o 49.3%.
agent_test: Compare at equal tokens a long-thinking base vs our scaffold on the same base.

claim: Retrieval or search helps modestly: Med-Gemini with one search iteration gained about 4 points top-10 on NEJM CPC; McDuff's search arm gained 8 to 11 points over unaided clinicians.
agent_test: Test retrieval on vs off at equal tokens.

claim: Elicitation penalty is not specific to old open models: GPT-4o drops from 89.0% to 60.9% (MC) and 78.4% to 30.3% (free response) when 218 text vignettes become patient-AI conversations; GPT-4 on iMedQA falls 79.7% to 54.5% with only initial info and interactive asking adds almost nothing (55.4%).
agent_test: Run the agent on CPC cases with full text vs a patient simulator that can answer any question the source supports; report the drop.

claim: A GPT-4o simulated patient overstates how well models handle real, lossy input: simulated users scored 57.3% disposition and 60.7% conditions vs humans at most 34.5% conditions, and simulator scores barely predicted human scores.
agent_test: Do not trust a simulated patient to rank agent variants; check against at least one human-played run.

claim: Confidence-gated abstention ('ask more when unsure') recovers part of the elicitation loss: MediQ best interactive GPT-4 66.1% vs basic 55.4% vs full-info 79.7% on iMedQA; the abstract's +22.3% could not be reproduced from the table.
agent_test: Add an explicit sufficiency check before answering or asking.

claim: No published study isolates MAI-DxO's challenger or other roles, or equalises tokens against the same base model; ensemble gain (85.5% vs 81.9%) mixes sampling with aggregation.
agent_test: Own ablation: single pass vs panel vs self-consistency at equal tokens, drop-one-role.

claim: At equal tokens, multi-agent structure helps on decomposable tasks and hurts on sequential ones (Finance Agent +80.8% centralised; PlanCraft -39.1% to -70.0%; mean change -0.3%). Debate often fails to beat CoT and self-consistency. Evidence is from non-medical tasks.
agent_test: Treat panels as a hypothesis for diagnosis; measure against self-consistency.

claim: A confident but wrong argument can derail a multi-agent debate (accuracy -10 to -40%, wrong consensus +30%), and more agents or rounds do not fix it. A challenger role must be tied to evidence, not persuasion.
agent_test: Require the challenger to name a discriminating test or finding; test against a planted wrong challenger.

claim: Prompt-planted bias lowers medical-QA accuracy for current models, and a reasoning mode does not reliably protect: Gemini-2.5-Flash fell to 47.4-86.1% on unpublished bias prompts; Llama-3.3-70B and Gemini were more vulnerable to several biases with reasoning on. Debiasing and few-shot prompts helped all three; anchoring on a wrong prior hypothesis was not directly tested.
agent_test: Test the agent with a planted wrong early hypothesis, with and without a challenger.

claim: Anchoring-bias failure rates on hard emergency cases range 6.9% to 26.4% across six 2025 models, and most dangerous outputs are stochastic (31 of 34), so repeat sampling catches failures that single runs hide.
agent_test: Sample the final answer several times and flag disagreement.

claim: Verbalised confidence has some signal for GPT-4o-class models (83.2% accuracy at confidence 5 vs 16.7% below 3) but is compressed near the top and absent in most models; 9 of 12 models never said 'I don't know'. Accuracy and calibration can diverge between current models (ECE 0.251 vs 0.083). No test on CPC top-1 exists.
agent_test: Measure confidence-vs-correctness on CPC top-1 for our agent before using confidence as a stop rule.

claim: How physicians type the case into an LLM (copy-paste, selective, summary, short query) did not predict score; output format and prompting remain untested as causes of the human-plus-LLM failure. A short ranked list raised top-3 (62.3% to 74.6%) but not top-1 (P=.08) in a 13-physician simulation.
agent_test: Compare free-form vs short ranked structured output in a human-in-loop pilot, if ever needed.

claim: Searches on 2026-11-01 found no study of pre/post-cutoff accuracy on real records, no rerank or discrimination stage tested on CPC top-1, and no retest of forced-differential or Bayesian prompts on current reasoning models. The search path was limited (quota exhausted, arXiv and Semantic Scholar rate-limited), so this is weak evidence of absence.
agent_test: Retry these three searches when quota returns.
